questions.title: Why beta does not determine realized KL
questions.prompt: Two DPO runs use the same $\beta$ but different learning rates, epoch counts, and data. Must they end with the same KL to the reference?
questions.explanation: No. In the variational objective $\beta$ prices KL; in DPO it scales the classification logit. Realized drift depends on data, log-probability normalization, optimizer, update count, and parameterization. Measure KL separately under a fixed protocol.

questions.title: Zero reference support
questions.prompt: For one completion $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)=0$ while the current policy assigns positive probability. What happens to forward KL and the DPO ratio?
questions.explanation: Forward KL is infinite for policy mass outside reference support, and $\log(\pi_\theta/\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})$ is not finite. Softmax models usually have positive mathematical probabilities, but hard masks, truncation, or numerical underflow can create effective zeros; support is part of the contract.

questions.title: cDPO is not automatically Robust DPO
questions.prompt: Why can label smoothing with $\varepsilon$ not be called an unbiased noise correction without qualification?
questions.explanation: cDPO mixes positive and flipped binary losses as a conservative heuristic. Robust DPO derives a particular correction under a symmetric label-flip model. Neither repairs a systematically wrong rubric, leakage, or distribution shift.

questions.title: Stale fixed pairs
questions.prompt: After several epochs the policy nearly perfectly separates old pairs, but fresh current-policy responses show new errors. What should be done?
questions.explanation: Stop drawing conclusions from old pair accuracy, collect fresh current-policy candidates, label or verify them, re-check base capabilities, and consider iterative DPO or online RL. A fixed set need not remain representative.

questions.title: Margin up, chosen logp down
questions.prompt: Mean DPO margin rises from 0.2 to 1.1 while mean `logps/chosen` falls. Is that a contradiction?
questions.explanation: No. DPO optimizes a relative reference-corrected gap. The rejected completion may lose likelihood faster, while unlabelled completions gain mass. Track chosen and rejected logp separately and evaluate fresh generations independently.

questions.title: Truncating one completion
questions.prompt: The chosen completion is cut at 256 tokens while the rejected completion fits in 90. Can the pair be treated as an ordinary DPO example?
questions.explanation: Only if the truncation rule was defined in advance and the truncated strings are the actual preference objects. Otherwise the label concerns a different sequence than the loss. Filter or re-label such pairs and report truncation rates.

questions.title: Choose from the data contract
questions.prompt: You have separate desirable and undesirable completions but no same-prompt pairs. What is the sound first choice: DPO, KTO, or artificial pairing?
questions.explanation: Use a method matching the observed feedback, such as KTO or another binary objective. Pairing unrelated prompts changes the question and breaks the prompt-dependent normalizer cancellation behind DPO.

questions.title: UltraFeedback provenance
questions.prompt: May `trl-lib/ultrafeedback_binarized` be described as direct human preference data?
questions.explanation: No. It is a derivative of UltraFeedback with synthetic model-generated feedback. It is useful for engineering practice, but the feedback provenance, candidate generators, and binarization must be stated.

questions.title: A shared chat template is mathematical
questions.prompt: Why must policy and reference log-probabilities use the same chat template and response mask?
questions.explanation: Otherwise $\log\pi_\theta-\log\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ compares different token sequences or token sets. The margin no longer implements the DPO formula and may measure formatting rather than preference.
